articles.headline: NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 7.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第7週：日曜日の試合から得られた大きな教訓、疑問点、そしてファンタジー視点での考察
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationのリポーターたちが、日曜日の各試合で生じた最大の疑問に答えながら、すべての展開を振り返ります。第7週から得られた知見がこちらです。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Paris between the Saints and the Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

Later in the afternoon, the Buccaneers dominated the Panthers in QB Baker Mayfield's return, the Vikings remained undefeated and the Bengals handled business in Baltimore. 

In the evening slate, the Broncos stole a win in Arizona, and the Lions outlasted the visiting Packers in a duel. 

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

LAR-LV | GB-DET | DEN-ARI

 NYG-HOU | TB-CAR | CLE-TEN

MIA-NYJ | SF-ATL | CIN-BAL 

IND-MIN | PIT-NO

Catch up on Thursday's game:

NE-CHI

L.A. Rams 35, Las Vegas 21

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams

Will leaning on Puka Nacua and tight ends be the Rams' offensive identity without Davante Adams? Outside of Nacua, just one Rams wide receiver had a catch: Konata Mumpfield, for 15 yards. Instead, the Rams turned to their tight ends (Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee) and their running backs (Kyren Williams and Blake Corum). It led to their highest-scoring game of the season. Most of the points came in the first half, when Los Angeles scored on four-straight possessions. The Rams will be without Adams, who injured a hamstring in Week 6, for another five to nine weeks.

Key stat to know: After fumbling on the Rams' second drive of the second half, Williams has nine lost fumbles since becoming the Rams starter in 2023. According to ESPN Research, that is the most of any running back over the span. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Raiders

Is the clock ticking on Kirk Cousins' time as a starter? Not necessarily. The Raiders have lost four straight and are below .500 for the first time this season. Sure, Cousins didn't have his best game overall. He missed open targets a fair amount of time, and his lack of mobility was noticeable. But he has not been the sole problem during his team's losing skid. He threw a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter, increasing his season total to 16. Cousins has his limitations, which are exposed when frequently blitzed, as he was Sunday. At the same time, he hasn't done anything major that's worth making a switch for No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza.

Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's seat might start feeling a bit warm. The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points for the fourth straight game. articles.headline: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 7: McCarthy-led Giants are NFC East favorites?
articles.description: Are Giants playoff bound? Are Vikings the NFC top seed? How bad do 49ers need Mike Evans back? We're judging overreactions to Sunday's games.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第7週の過剰反応を判定：マッカーシー率いるジャイアンツがNFC東地区の本命か？
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツはプレーオフ進出か？バイキングスがNFCのトップシードになるのか？49ersにとってマイク・エバンスの復帰はどれほど切実か？日曜日の試合に対する過剰な反応を検証します。
articles.body:
Well, if one of your Week 6 takeaways was that the Texans were going to be just fine after all, you might have been overreacting.

That's the beauty of the middle of the NFL season, isn't it? Just when we think we have stuff figured out, the league still shows the ability to surprise us. The Falcons handed the 49ers their first loss of the season. The Steelers and Browns are both 5-2 and tied for first place in the AFC North. J.J. McCarthy is winning road games for the Giants.

So we keep doing this weekly exercise here because it's fun, and we do it fully aware that we have no idea what the rest of the season -- or even next week! -- will bring.

So here's our Week 7 overreactions column, where we look at five potential takeaways from all the action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the bottom.

Jump to:

McCarthy can lead Giants to playoffs?

49ers can't afford to be without Evans?

Bengals need to trade for a star RB?

Vikings will be the NFC's top seed?

Nix, Broncos offense are back?

Fantasy overreactions

J.J. McCarthy can lead the Giants to the playoffs

Acquired from the Vikings in a trade almost a month ago, McCarthy got his first start for the Giants on Sunday in Houston. He threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter the week before in a relief effort against the Saints, which was enough to earn him the No. 1 spot on the Giants' QB depth chart for Week 7. He drew a tough assignment against Houston's fearsome defense, but Giants coach John Harbaugh decided McCarthy was up for it, and he was right.

McCarthy looked extremely comfortable and confident all day, ripping throws into tight windows and operating the offense cleanly. Giants coaches wanted to see a smooth operation, and after the game Harbaugh pointed out that there were no procedural penalties or glaring errors. The run game sprang to life, gaining 188 yards on 34 carries and winning the game in overtime when Cam Skattebo got New York into field goal range with a 42-yard run and Devin Singletary rendered the field goal unnecessary with a 30-yard touchdown run on the next play. McCarthy was 20-for-28 for 252 yards and no turnovers. He looked very much like he belonged.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

No one has wanted to take this seriously, but the first-place Giants are 4-2-1 and will carry at least a 1.5-game NFC East lead into Week 8 regardless of what happens between the Cowboys and Eagles on Monday night. Harbaugh has made a major difference in his first season as Giants head coach. They're avoiding mistakes, overcoming injuries and finding ways to win. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy called an outstanding game for McCarthy. Skattebo bounced back after last week's soft benching and said after the game that he agreed with and appreciated the way it was handled by the coaching staff. articles.headline: Haliburton has 24 points and 10 assists as the Pacers beat the winless Nets 136-109
articles.description: — Tyrese Haliburton had 24 points, 10 assists and an All-Star Game-worthy dunk as the Indiana Pacers hammered the Brooklyn Nets 136-109 on Sunday night.
articles.headlineJa: ハリバートンが24得点10アシストを記録し、ペイサーズが無勝のネッツに136-109で快勝
articles.descriptionJa: タイリーズ・ハリバートンが24得点10アシストを挙げ、オールスターゲーム級のダンクを披露。インディアナ・ペイサーズが日曜夜、ブルックリン・ネッツを136-109で圧倒しました。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Tyrese Haliburton had 24 points, 10 assists and an All-Star Game-worthy dunk as the Indiana Pacers hammered the Brooklyn Nets 136-109 on Sunday night.


              The Pacers shot 58% (49 for 85) from the field, including 49% (21 for 43) from 3-point distance.


              Haliburton shot 8 for 13 from the field, Pascal Siakam added 21 points and Obi Toppin chipped in 16 off the bench.


              Reserve guard Nolan Traore had 17 points for Brooklyn, which has lost its first three games of the season.


              Indiana trailed by two points at the end of the first quarter before outscoring the Nets 41-30 in the second period to take a 65-56 lead at the break. The Pacers shot 58% from the field and 42% beyond the 3-point line in the first half.


              The Pacers continued their good rhythm in the third quarter by blitzing the Nets 37-24 for a 98-74 advantage heading into the final period.


              Haliburton, who missed last season while recovering from a torn right Achilles tendon, provided the highlight of the third quarter.


              With 7:17 remaining, Julius Randle lost control of the ball at the top of the arc and Aaron Nesmith dove for it before Siakam picked it up and found a wide-open Haliburton, who bounced the ball to himself in front of the free throw line and threw down two-handed dunk that drew the approval of his teammates.


              Ivica Zubac was removed from the game after he sprained his left ankle with 4:57 left in the first quarter after he stepped on Kelly Oubre’s foot while chasing down a rebound.


              Up next
              Pacers: Visit the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday night.


              Nets: Visit the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic scores NBA season-high 52 points, with 8 3s, in Lakers' win vs. Jazz
articles.description: Luka Doncic scored 52 points, hitting eight 3-pointers, to lead the Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Jazz on Sunday. It was the first 50-point game this season in the NBA.
articles.headlineJa: ルカ・ドンチッチが3ポイントシュート8本を含む今季NBA最多の52得点を記録し、レイカーズがジャズに勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日、ルカ・ドンチッチが8本の3ポイントシュートを沈め52得点を記録し、レイカーズを132-123でのジャズ戦勝利に導きました。これは今シーズンのNBAで初の50得点試合となりました。
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY -- Luka Doncic scored 52 points, hitting eight 3-pointers, to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday.

In the first 50-point game this season in the NBA, Doncic made several big baskets late in the fourth quarter to help the Lakers win for the eighth time in their last nine games against Utah. He finished off a 14-5 go-ahead run with back-to-back 3s that gave Los Angeles a 127-121 lead with 1:42 left.

Doncic also had 10 assists and seven rebounds. Austin Reaves added 29 points for the Lakers. The pair combined to shoot 21-of-24 on free throws.

Walker Kessler had only two points and seven rebounds in his first game back in Utah after being sent to Los Angeles in a sign-and-trade deal in July.

Lauri Markkanen scored 28 points to lead the Jazz, who blew an 18-point second-quarter lead.

Keyonte George had 24 points, nine rebounds, and 10 assists for the Jazz. Jaren Jackson Jr. added 20 points while Ace Bailey chipped in 17 points and 12 rebounds.

Doncic hit a step-back 3-pointer with 4.1 seconds left in the half to give the Lakers their first lead at 74-71.

The Lakers improved to 3-0 with their next game at home against the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Week 7 winners and losers: Pollard, Burrow lead the way; Purdy, Henry struggle
articles.description: Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers came up big in Week 7, while Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Nico Collins all had quiet days.
articles.headlineJa: 第7週の勝者と敗者：ポラードとバロウが躍進、パーディーとヘンリーは苦戦
articles.descriptionJa: 第7週はトニー・ポラード、ジョー・バロウ、ゼイ・フラワーズが大きく貢献した一方、ブロック・パーディー、デリック・ヘンリー、ニコ・コリンズは静かな一日となりました。
articles.body:
Week 7 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured big games by Tony Pollard, Joe Burrow and Zay Flowers. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy, Derrick Henry and Nico Collins all had very quiet days.

So, who were the big winners and losers around the league during the seventh week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Michael F. Florio offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 7

1. Tony Pollard, RB, Tennessee Titans

Pollard might be the player of the week, turning 25 carries into 129 yards and three touchdowns. He had scored two touchdowns in his previous 10 games combined. He recorded a season high in yards and totaled his third most in a game as a Titan. He also caught all three of his targets for 26 yards and finished with 36.5 fantasy points. Pollard has averaged 19 touches per game since Week 2, which has him in play weekly as an RB2 or flex option. He is a volume play against a vastly improved Bengals rush defense next week. -- Florio

2. Joe Burrow, QB; Tee Higgins, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Burrow scored a season-high 28.88 points in Sunday's win over the Ravens, throwing for 292 yards and four touchdowns. After a slow start to the year, Burrow has scored 22 or more points in four straight games, with three or more touchdowns in three of his past four. Higgins' 26.8 points were also a season high (he caught 6 of 7 targets for 148 yards and a touchdown), which gives him 21 or more points in three of his past four games. With Burrow's recent level of play, managers can view him as a top-five QB for Week 8, while Higgins moves up the WR2 ranks. -- Bowen

3. Zay Flowers, WR, Baltimore Ravens

With backup quarterback Tyler Huntley getting another start, Flowers produced a season-best 27.7 points in the loss to the Bengals. Flowers caught 8 of 11 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown, and he has posted 25 or more points in three of six games played. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) potentially returning next week in a positive matchup versus the Bills' defense, Flowers will be in my WR1 rankings. -- Bowen

4. Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Judkins scored a season-high 23.4 points in Sunday's win over the Titans, rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries, plus a reception for 8 yards. Yes, Judkins is a touchdown-dependent player in the lineup, but he has had two goal-to-go rushes in two of his past three games and he sees the Steelers' defense again in Week 8. Back in the Week 4 game versus Pittsburgh, Judkins scored 21.6 fantasy points with 96 total yards and a touchdown on 23 touches. He should be locked in as a RB2 next week. -- Bowen

5. Jameson Williams, WR, Detroit Lions

articles.headline: Mourinho primes Madrid for statement win over Barça to blow LaLiga title race wide open
articles.description: Real Madrid haven't convinced this season, but José Mourinho's game plan overwhelmed Barça, and Los Blancos' 2-1 win brings them into the title race.
articles.body:
BARCELONA, Spain -- Kylian Mbappé scored twice as Real Madrid stunned Barcelona 2-1 at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday to end the Catalan side's perfect start to the season. Mbappé struck the winner in the 87th minute after good work from Jude Bellingham and Eduardo Camavinga as Madrid cut the gap between themselves and league leaders Barça to three points.

Madrid had gone into the game as underdogs given the two teams' respective starts to the campaign but silenced the home fans just before the break when Mbappé capitalized on a Gerard Martín error.

Barça fought back in the second half. Raphinha's 15th goal of the campaign drew them level from a well-worked corner in the 61st minute, and from there they pushed for a winner.

Andriy Lunin, in for the ill Thibaut Courtois in Madrid's goal, made a fine stop from a Martín header and Lamine Yamal whisked wide from distance. However, Madrid remained a threat on the break, and they sealed all three points late on when Bellingham and Camavinga combined after Gabriel Jesus lost the ball to tee up a tap in for Mbappé.

Madrid move on to 24 points from their 10 games this season, one behind second-placed Atlético Madrid and three back from leaders Barça, whose nine-game winning streak in the league is now over. -- Sam Marsden

Mourinho blows title race wide open

José Mourinho had insisted prematch that this Clásico wouldn't deliver a verdict on whether his Madrid team can win things this season. The answer was already clear, he said, with no further proof required: "Madrid with Mourinho wins trophies."

A Clásico win isn't a trophy. There's a long way to go between now and May, but this was a huge test for Mourinho's Madrid: their biggest game yet, away from home, against the -- until the full-time whistle blew -- unbeaten LaLiga leaders. And it's a test Madrid passed, superbly.

They were competitive throughout, well organized and structured out of possession, and always dangerous on the counterattack. This was Mourinho's Madrid, the kind of team that had only shown itself in flashes this season, now fully formed.

"I think it was a great game," Mourinho said after the match. "A game at a high level, a game that the world which loves football stopped to see. And they weren't let down, with two teams that played to win.

"In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organized, focused, with a lot of courage, playing an opponent that presses you a lot. ... For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent."

Mourinho got everything right. His team selection delivered, with the coach's key decisions -- Bernardo Silva as a surprise partner for Aurélien Tchouaméni in central midfield, Arda Güler,outstanding again on the right, and Federico Valverde at right back until he was forced off injured -- paying off.

articles.headline: Pedri says Barcelona paid for stupid mistakes in loss to Real Madrid
articles.description: Midfielder Pedri lamented stupid makes and slowness on the ball as Barcelona's perfect start to the LaLiga season was ended by Real Madrid in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.
articles.body:
Midfielder Pedri lamented stupid makes and slowness on the ball as Barcelona's perfect start to the LaLiga season was ended by Real Madrid in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.

Kylian Mbappé scored twice either side of Raphinha's equaliser in the 2-1 win for Jose Mourinho's side, including an 87th-minute goal, as Madrid halted Barça's winning streak in the league at nine games to move within three points of Hansi Flick's team at the top of the table.

"In general, we didn't play well," Pedri told DAZN. "We were not ourselves in the first half. There are a lot of things we could have done better.

"We got back on level terms in the second half, but we did not defend the second goal well -- from a transition, as well, which we knew they could do.

"But, above all, in the first half we were really slow, we lost the ball stupidly a lot and you pay for those mistakes."

Mbappé gave Madrid a first-half lead when he turned home from close range after a poor clearance from Gerard Martín, but Barça fought back after the break through Raphinha's 15th goal of the campaign.

However, with Barça pushing for a winner late on, they left space in behind which Madrid took advantage of, breaking through with Eduardo Camavinga, who teed up Mbappé for his second of the evening and his 100th goal for Los Blancos.

It completed a miserable week for Barça. After 11 consecutive victories in all competitions, they have now lost back-to-back games after also losing 4-2 at Paris Saint-Germain last Tuesday in the Champions League.

Flick refused to label the defeats a "reality check," instead saying tiredness was the reason for the losses.

"It's two defeats so of course we are not happy; we are disappointed," Flick said in the post-game news conference. "The first half was not good. The second half, after the equaliser, was better. I think also we controlled the game. We missed a little bit of luck. But they played well, they didn't give us much space.

"Also, you could see today we missed the freshness. It's about this. It's the first defeat in LaLiga. We won nine in a row [in the league]. But it happens, defeats are a part of the game."

Flick said the results against PSG and Madrid will "not create doubts" around his team, instead doubling down on the fatigue his players are suffering and a defensive injury list which includes Andreas Christensen, Jules Koundé and Eric García -- and now Xavi Espart, who was taken off in the first half of the Clásico.

"No, no [doubts], that is clear," he added. "Everyone knows the situation, that we don't play very good. But in the big games, small things are important. They decide the games.

"We played against an opponent that has huge quality. They were better against the ball than in the Clásico in previous years.

"Like I said, you saw today we missed the freshness. After these weeks, it was not easy for my players. We have to now focus again and recover well.

articles.headline: José Mourinho not satisfied with just beating Barcelona: 'Real Madrid play to win the league'
articles.description: José Mourinho said he's setting his sights even higher after Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in Sunday's Clásico, saying "Real Madrid play to win the league, not to win at Camp Nou."
articles.body:
José Mourinho said he's setting his sights even higher after Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in Sunday's Clásico, saying "Real Madrid play to win the league, not to win at Camp Nou."

Kylian Mbappé scored twice -- including a dramatic 87th-minute winner -- to give Madrid the victory in LaLiga, closing the gap between the two sides at the top of the table to just three points.

Mourinho's team have now won five games in a row in all competitions, but speaking in his post-match news conference, the coach insisted that he's not getting carried away with their form.

"This is a great win, but when we get back to work, I'm not going to let anyone have their head in the clouds," Mourinho said. "If we win today and lose at El Sardinero [away at Racing Santander next weekend]... Real Madrid don't play to win at Camp Nou, but rather to win the league. We have to keep going."

Mbappé put Madrid ahead in the 41st minute on Sunday, as defender Gerard Martín's attempted clearance rebounded off the forward and into the net.

Raphinha levelled, before Mbappé finished off a stunning Madrid counterattack late on, with substitute Eduardo Camavinga providing the assist.

"I think it was a great game," Mourinho said. "A game at a high level, a game which the world that loves football stopped to see, and they weren't let down... In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage.

"For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. The boys deserve it."

Reserve goalkeeper Andriy Lunin had to step in for Thibaut Courtois at Camp Nou, who had the flu.

"The only thing I said to Lunin before the game was: you train to play, not to be on the bench," Mourinho said. "We have the best keeper in the world, but today we weren't crying before the game because Thibaut couldn't play. The group is strong."

Mourinho confirmed captain Federico Valverde had picked up an injury early in the match, but opted to continue playing to help his teammates.

"Valverde played injured for over 40 minutes," he said. "He got injured, he wanted to carry on. He wanted to go to the limit. He gave everything on the field."

articles.headline: Sixers overrule Embiid, sit center with plantar fasciitis management
articles.description: Despite publicly calling to play Sunday against the Pistons, the 76ers decided to sit Joel Embiid due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
articles.headlineJa: シックスターズ、エンビードの意向を覆し、足底筋膜炎のケアのためセンターを欠場させる
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のピストンズ戦への出場を公言していたものの、76ersは右足の足底筋膜炎のケアのため、ジョエル・エンビードを欠場させることを決定した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- A day after Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid asked reporters to campaign for him to play in Sunday's game against Detroit -- the second of the Sixers' first back-to-back this season -- the 76ers ruled out Embiid for Sunday night's game against the Detroit Pistons with right foot plantar fasciitis management. ​

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said with a smile after Saturday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

 

The Sixers decided against Embiid's wishes, as they look to keep the former MVP healthy for a long season. Embiid, plagued by various injuries, has averaged just 49 games per season over his 10 years.

In their win over the Bucks on Saturday, Embiid had his tenth career triple-double, finishing with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Having him sidelined is a significant blow to the Sixers' already thin frontcourt.

Philadelphia also ruled out big men Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad). Walker injured his left knee in Saturday's win, exiting the game in the third quarter. That leaves Adem Bona as the team's only true center active on Sunday. Forward Dean Wade, who made his season debut on Saturday, will likely play some center, and LeBron James, who missed Saturday's game with sciatica management, has no injury designation and can also help out at the center spot.

The Pistons will be without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who the team said has a hamstring injury and will be out for at least two weeks.

articles.headline: Pistons C Jalen Duren out at least two weeks with hamstring strain
articles.description: Pistons center Jalen Duren, who signed a five-year extension earlier this month, will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday.

Duren suffered the injury in the first half of Friday's win over the Miami Heat. He played only 10 minutes before leaving the game.

"It's tough when you lose a guy that means as much to us as JD does," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before Sunday's game in Philadelphia. "It's tough. Tough for him. Trying to come back and get himself situated to start the year. You miss those days. It's obviously a little bit difficult for us."

Duren's offseason was marked by a lengthy standoff with the Pistons over a contract extension. He missed media day and the first few practices of training camp before ultimately signing a five-year, $200 million deal.

Last season, he averaged a career high in points (19.5 PPG), made his first All-Star team and was named to the All-NBA third team as the Pistons earned the top seed in the Eastern Conference. But he struggled mightily in the postseason, dropping to 10.2 points per game in 14 playoff games before Detroit's second-round exit.

Duren scored 22 points with nine rebounds in Detroit's season-opening win over the Boston Celtics.

Information from The Associated Press and ESPN's Jamal Collier was used in this report.

articles.headline: Barcelona vs. Real Madrid player ratings as Kylian Mbappé sinks out-of-sorts hosts
articles.description: A brace from Kylian Mbappé -- the latter his 100th goal for the club -- claimed a famous victory for Real Madrid over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナ対レアル・マドリードの選手評：キリアン・エムバペが不調のホームチームを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペが2得点（クラブでの通算100ゴール目）を挙げ、レアル・マドリードはスポティファイ・カンプ・ノウでのバルセロナ戦で劇的な勝利を飾った。
articles.body:
A brace from Kylian Mbappé -- the latter his 100th goal for the club -- claimed a famous victory for Real Madrid over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou.

Having won every game so far in LaLiga, Barcelona looked extremely vulnerable to the Frenchman's pace in behind and eventually paid the price, letting Madrid back into the title race when they could, realistically, have been out of sight already.

Here, ESPN rates both sets of players after a dramatic Clásico.

Barcelona

Manager rating (out of 10)

Hansi Flick, 4 -- A rare off night for one of the best managers in the world. Barcelona have obviously had wonderful results playing a high line so far this season but Mbappé's pace allowed him to get in behind almost at will, and only poor service to the Frenchman prevented him getting even more chances.

Player ratings (1-10; 10 = best, 5 = average)

GK Joan García, 5 -- Couldn't have done much about either of the goals. Pulled off a couple of smart saves, most notably to deny Arda Güler.

RB Xaxi Espart, 5 -- Showed a couple of neat touches but withdrawn with an injury on the half-hour mark.

CB Pau Cubarsí, 4 -- Not his usual assured self. Struggled with Mbappé's pace in behind as Barcelona played a very high line. Needed Gerard Martín to bail him out when he dived in on Bellingham on the halfway line, missed the ball and presented Madrid with a two-on-one. Also caught out for Mbappé's winner.

CB Gerard Martín, 6 -- Struggled in the first half, and made a poor mistake for the opening goal, even if it was a little unfortunate. But looked a different player in the second and snuffed out a glorious chance for Bellingham and Mbappé, positioning his body perfectly between them when he was left all alone to deal with their counter-attack. Could have scored, but for a brilliant Lunin save.

LB João Cancelo, 4 -- Looked less comfortable when moved to right back after Xavi Espart's injury. Could not keep up with Yan Diomande's blistering speed.

DM Rodri, 5 -- As the anchor in Barcelona's midfield, he may feel a little disappointed with how open Barcelona were in the 15-minute period either side of halftime. Showed some neat touches on the ball, especially as the hosts began to dominate in the closing stages.

DM Pedri, 6 -- Struggled to assert himself in the first half but pulled out a nice assist in the second and looked much-improved from then on. Was key to Barcelona keeping the pressure on in the closing stages.

RW Lamine Yamal, 6 -- Marc Cucurella looked to have been told by Mourinho to antagonise the young winger, and it certainly worked in the first half. Had the perfect chance to level the scoring almost instantly after Mbappé's opener but shanked his finish well wide. Improved in the second and had a number of decent efforts, but overall will be disappointed he could not take his sparkling form into this game.

AM Fermín López, 6 -- Classy footballer. Carried the ball well through midfield but struggled to impact the game in the final third.

articles.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard to miss Wolves game with knee swelling
articles.description: Raptors star Kawhi Leonard is out for Sunday night's game against the Timberwolves due to left knee swelling.
articles.headlineJa: ラプターズのカワイ・レナード、膝の腫れによりウルブズ戦を欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ラプターズのスター、カワイ・レナードは、左膝の腫れのため日曜夜のティンバーウルブズ戦を欠場する。
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard will miss his first game this season due to what the Toronto Raptors are calling left knee swelling.

The All-NBA forward will miss Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

In his first season back with the Raptors since helping to win the franchise's first NBA championship in 2019, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals in two games this season.

Leonard has an extensive history of right knee issues including an ACL tear in 2021 and a meniscus tear in 2023. The LA Clippers, who traded Leonard to Toronto before the season, load-managed Leonard for much of his tenure there due to issues with the knee.
